nodes.name: Catalyst ink preparation
nodes.procedure: Inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectroscopy (ICP-AES) measurements show the concentrations of Au and Ru in the Au@Ru colloidal solutions in Supplementary Table 3. The Au@Ru colloidal solution was condensed to 1.5 mg mL⁻¹ (relative to Ru). 50 μL of condensed Au@Ru sol was mixed with 175 μL isopropanol and 25 μL Nafion (2 wt%). 0.75 mg of Vulcan XC-72R (Cabot Co.) was then added to the solution and sonicated for 30 min (Vulcan XC acted as structural support for the Au@Ru NPs). For the Au@Ru/C catalyst ink, a Ru loading of 0.3 mg mL⁻¹ was used. 50 μL of the catalyst ink was then drop-cast onto the surface of the carbon cloth and dried naturally before electrochemical measurements.

First, we tested the HER performance of 55 nm Au and 55 nm Au@2.5 nm Ru NPs in a 0.1 M NaOH solution (pH ~13). As shown in Fig. 2a, the Au@Ru NPs have an overpotential of ∼176 mV at a current density of −10 mA cm−2 while Au NPs have far inferior HER performance under the same conditions.

First, we tested the HER performance of 55 nm Au and 55 nm Au@2.5 nm Ru NPs in a 0.1 M NaOH solution (pH ~13). As shown in Fig. 2a, the Au@Ru NPs have an overpotential of ∼176 mV at a current density of −10 mA cm−2 while Au NPs have far inferior HER performance under the same conditions.

nodes.description: HER performance comparison of original, reduced, and oxidized Ru surfaces in 0.1 M NaOH
nodes.source_text: The overpotentials of HER at oxidized, original, and reduced Ru surfaces are around 143, 176, and 215 mV at the current density of −10 mA cm−2 in a 0.1 M NaOH solution (Fig. 3c). Tafel slopes are 114.8, 133.6, and 146.5 mV dec−1. The ECSA of original, reduced, and oxidized Ru surfaces are 1236, 1020, and 977 cm². The chromatographic test results showed that the hydrogen yield was ... 157.1 ppm, 240.0 ppm, and 424.9 ppm for reduced, original, and oxidized Ru respectively

We also tested the HER performance of Au@Ru NPs in a typical 1.0 M KOH solution and 1.0 M NaOH solution (Supplementary Fig. 5). The overpotentials of alkaline HER in 1.0 M KOH and NaOH are similar (67 mV)

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show uniform size and good dispersibility of Au@Ru NPs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Supplementary Fig. 1a, b shows the SEM and TEM images of the synthesized Au@Ru NPs, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM images confirm Au core diameter of ~55 nm and Ru shell thickness of ~2.5 nm with no obvious pinholes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The NPs possessed a uniform size and good dispersibility with a diameter of the Au core of ∼55 nm and a thickness of the Ru shell of ∼2.5 nm, and no obvious pinholes can be observed.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM and elemental mapping show uniform distribution of Au and Ru in the NPs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HAADF-STEM and elemental mapping images show the uniform distribution of Au and Ru in the NPs (Fig. 1b–e).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS spectra of Ru 3p and O 1s show oxidation of the most outer layer of the Ru shell under atmospheric conditions.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Supplementary Fig. 4, XPS spectra of the Ru 3p and O 1s electrons of the Au@Ru nanocatalysts show the oxidation of the most out-layer of the Ru shell under atmospheric conditions.

nodes.characterization_summary: CVs in non-faradaic region (0.10-0.20 V) at different scan rates determine ECSA of 1236 cm² (original), 1020 cm² (reduced), and 977 cm² (oxidized) Ru surfaces with negligible differences.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The ECSA of original, reduced, and oxidized Ru surfaces are 1236, 1020, and 977 cm², showing the negligible difference in ECSA of the catalysts after the test.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-AES measurements show concentrations of Au and Ru in Au@Ru colloidal solutions.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectroscopy (ICP-AES) measurements show the concentrations of Au and Ru in the Au@Ru colloidal solutions in Supplementary Table 3.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman reveals RuOx surface oxide at ~516 cm⁻¹, two distinct *H species at ~1825 cm⁻¹ (Ru(0)) and ~1960 cm⁻¹ (Ru(n+)), *OH at ~715 cm⁻¹, and interfacial water structures on Au@Ru catalyst surfaces during alkaline HER.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Raman bands around 516, 715, 1825, 1960, and 3410 cm⁻¹ are observed... the Raman band around 516 cm⁻¹ remains stable... could be attributed to RuOx surface oxide... 1827 and 3420 cm⁻¹... Ru-H bond... 1950 cm⁻¹... Ru-H bond at oxidized Ru(n+) surfaces.
